# P3 synthetic Informer CUDA fixtures

These fixtures use no private or public dataset rows. They are generated by tools/reference/gen_p3_fixtures.py from the clean pinned Time-Series-Library checkout at 4e938a1767106324dd753b2a44832bf870a0252e (MIT, Copyright (c) 2021 THUML @ Tsinghua University).

The manifest binds the generator, source files, torch version/git identity, CUDA device and every artifact hash. Standard train/eval cases use B2, L12, H4, three variables, width8, two encoder layers with distillation, one decoder layer and dropout0. Sampling indices are injected into the unchanged upstream score/top-query/context/autograd method; ordinary model dropout is disabled for numerical comparison.

Each case contains initial parameters and buffers, inputs, final outputs, module traces, all 72 true MSE parameter gradients, an additional key-projection connectivity probe, resulting buffers and shared sampling indices. I64 upstream batch counters are normalized to U32 for the explicitly bounded FerroTS counter representation. operators.safetensors holds six prefix/pool/row-replacement forward-and-VJP references.

Generate and check using the existing frozen reference environment:

```bash
uv run --frozen --project tools/reference python tools/reference/gen_p3_fixtures.py --device cuda:1
uv run --frozen --project tools/reference python tools/reference/gen_p3_fixtures.py --device cuda:1 --check
```

Generation requires CUDA and the exact recorded torch pin. The check compares tensor content bitwise and rechecks the manifest. Model comparisons use atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4. These small fixtures do not replace formal training, D4, memory/complexity measurements, or the independent private metric recomputation.

The bare upstream squeeze/log-length edge behavior is not claimed as an unmodified B/head=1 or L=1 reference. FerroTS's shape-safe boundary behavior and deterministic cutoff ties are tested separately.
